thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT - Router 504 spike detected (severity=P2). Service: router, affected route: /v1/generate (dedicated-nyc). Symptoms: elevated 504/502, increased retries, customer errors reported. Auto-escalated to #eng-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/router-fallback

Sara M: acked, I'm on it. Which pools are failing? Any confirmed customer impact yet? :eyes:

Chris L: seeing 504 spike starting ~1779998700. Error rate concentrated on requests that hit dedicated-nyc pool and then got routed to fallback variants. Metrics: router_request_504{pool="dedicated-nyc"} up x10.

Deepak P: quick snapshot from Prometheus:
```
# promql
sum(rate(router_request_504[2m])) by (pool)
# result (sample)
// dedicated-nyc: 18.2
// dedicated-eu: 1.1
```
Also noticed router_pool_capacity_active{pool="dedicated-nyc"} == 0 while node_gpu_allocations{pool="dedicated-nyc"} == 32. Looks like the capacity gauge the router uses was reporting zero. My hunch: metric rename in the exporter after the deploy yesterday caused the router to read the wrong label/metric (so autoscaler scale decisions and routing logic thought pool was empty).

Tim G: if router thinks capacity=0, it will trigger fallback policies -> route to region fallback variants -> those variants then exceed quota or are incompatible and return 502/504, causing retries and blackhole loops. Need a quick mitigation: disable fallback routing for dedicated pools and pin traffic to healthy hosts while we fix the metric.

Chris L: agree. I'm going to disable the region fallback policy for dedicated pools and add a temporary route override to pin customers on dedicated-nyc to the current hostset. Doing in the console now.

Tim G: commands I'm running (PATCH to config service):
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://config.redwood/api/v1/router/policies/region-fallback \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"enabled_for_pools": ["non-dedicated"]}'
```
Then pin route:
```bash
curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/v1/router/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"pool":"dedicated-nyc","pin_hostset":"dedicated-nyc-current"}'
```

opsbot: deploy-job/patch-config started by Tim G — job id: dj-9923

opsbot: deploy-job/patch-config completed: SUCCESS (2.1s) :white_check_mark:

Chris L: after the override, 504 rate dropped 70% in the next 90s. Still seeing some errors from queued requests.

Deepak P: found root cause: exporter in dedicated-nyc had a small refactor yesterday that renamed pool_capacity_active -> pool_capacity_reporting. Router's metric selector wasn't updated, so it interpreted missing metric as zero. Also, fallback policy logic treats zero as severe and starts aggressive region fallback. We'll need a patch both to exporter and to improve router resilience to missing metrics.

Sara M: do we have customer impact list? Any high-volume customers on dedicated-nyc?

Eva R: Support report: 3 Dedicated customers reported elevated 504s since ~1779998700 — customers: zenmarket, scaleflow, docsnap. I've opened tickets and notified their CSMs. No host-level failures, CPU/GPU utilization looks normal; this was purely routing/metrics. Flagging potential SLO impact: zenmarket (p50 latency SLO) breached for ~7m.

Chris L: mitigation timeline: 1779998888 alert -> 1779999000 disable fallback -> 1779999150 pin hosts -> 1779999300 errors dropping. Continuing to monitor.

Deepak P: next actions: 1) roll a hotfix to the exporter in dedicated-nyc that restores the metric name; 2) add defensive logic in router to treat missing metric as 'unknown' not zero (short-term: fallback soft threshold); 3) postmortem and runbook update. I'll open the follow-up tickets.

Tim G: deploying exporter hotfix to dedicated-nyc now (small restart of exporter daemon).

eng-runtime-bot: deploy exporter-hotfix-dedicated-nyc started (uid: dep-774)

eng-runtime-bot: deploy exporter-hotfix-dedicated-nyc finished: SUCCESS — restart completed on all 8 nodes (duration 45s)

Chris L: after exporter fix, router_pool_capacity_active now reports correct value, autoscale signal stabilized. No further fallback loops observed. 504/502 rates back to baseline.

PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged and assigned to on-call team. Severity set to P2.

Eva R: Customer comms: I'll update the three affected customers and point them to the incident summary + ETA for postmortem.

Deepak P: handing off to Chris L for postmortem and timeline reconstruction. I'll add root cause details and suggested code diffs for exporter + router.

Chris L: will own the postmortem. Drafting timeline and adding remediation items:
- patch exporter to avoid renames or provide compatibility metric
- router: treat missing metrics as unknown, add circuit breaker before aggressive fallback
- extend CI to catch metric name changes (exporter->router contract tests)
- update runbook: add step to check metric existence before disabling fallbacks

Sara M: thanks team — nice quick mitigation. Marking as resolved for oncall now, continuing follow-up work in a dedicated ticket. :shipit: :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: RESOLVED - Router 504 spike mitigated. Root cause: metric rename in dedicated-nyc exporter caused router to misread pool capacity as zero and trigger aggressive fallback policies, which in turn created request blackholing and customer 504s. Severity: P2. Follow-up: eng-runtime/eng-platform to own exporter fix and router resilience improvements. Postmortem owner: Chris L. Link: https://redwood/incidents/1779998888

Sara M: closing handoff — oncall clear.
